<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commodity Prices, Exchange Rates, and Credit</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>At the end of 2014, our borrowing base was reduced from $65 million to $55 million as a result of the lenders&#8217; redetermination.&#160;&#160;At year-end 2014, our outstanding debt totaled $50 million.&#160;&#160;The amount that we can borrow under our Senior Secured Credit Facility is based on our lenders&#8217; evaluation of our Polish reserves, and the expected future cash flow from those reserves, denominated in U.S. dollars.&#160;&#160;All of the natural gas we produce in Poland is sold under gas sales agreements that are denominated in zlotys.&#160;&#160;At the time of each semiannual reserve redetermination, our lenders calculate the net cash flows expected to be generated during the remaining term of our loan, as denominated in dollars.&#160;&#160;Part of that calculation is an assumption by the lenders concerning future gas prices and exchange rates.&#160;&#160;These assumptions can have a significant impact on the estimated future net cash flows denominated in dollars.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>As we discussed above, the effect of a 6.0% price decrease in the Polish low-methane tariff in a borrowing base recalculation is straightforward.&#160;&#160;Equally important is the effect of exchange-rate changes.&#160;&#160;At the end of 2013, the exchange rate was 3.01 zlotys per dollar compared to 3.51 zlotys per dollar at the end of 2014.&#160;&#160;The use of the latter rate by our lenders, instead of the former rate, results in a 17% reduction of estimated future net cash flows, denominated in dollars, from our production.&#160;&#160;This is turn would have a negative effect on our borrowing base and could cause us either to be limited in our access to credit or to be required to make earlier than scheduled principal payments.&#160;&#160;These changes are outside our influence or control.&#160;&#160;Our next redetermination is scheduled for June 30, 2015.&#160;&#160;In the meantime, we are discussing with our lenders an amendment and restatement of our existing facility, which we hope to close before the next redetermination, and which would likely increase our borrowing base beyond the $55 million current level.&#160;&#160;However, should these discussions not result in an increased borrowing base or revisions to the amortization language of the existing credit agreement, then we would likely have to begin amortization of our loan in 2015, which would be&#160;&#160;sooner than the scheduled commitment reductions outlined in our Senior Secured Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;This amortization would substantially impair the amount of capital we would have available for additional capital expenditures.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Changes to Poland&#8217;s Hydrocarbon Legislation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In late 2012, the Polish government approved guidelines for new hydrocarbon legislation, including, among other things, higher royalties on hydrocarbons produced and a new cash flow tax based on the positive cumulate cash flow of exploration and development projects.&#160;&#160;The law was passed in 2014.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The new legislation is meant to increase governmental revenue from the oil and gas industry, with the stated intention for the total royalty and tax burden of an energy company to approach 40% of taxable income, which is approximately double that of the current fiscal regime.&#160;&#160;The new law became effective January 1, 2015; however, the first royalty increase is delayed until January 1, 2016.&#160;&#160;Beginning in 2016, the royalty on the gas we produce will increase from 5.18 PLN per thousand cubic meters of gas to 20.00 PLN per thousand cubic meters.&#160;&#160;On January 1, 2020, an additional royalty equal to 3% of the sales value of gas produced will become effective.&#160;&#160;The new royalty and tax structure would be applicable to all production, without regard to when the well was drilled or the relevant concession granted.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The tax on profits from hydrocarbon production, which is based on the positive cumulative cash flow of exploration and development projects, goes into effect on January 1, 2020.&#160;&#160;Each company subject to the tax is allowed to include all qualifying costs incurred between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2019, as part of a beginning cost pool.&#160;&#160;The new tax does not go into effect until the company&#8217;s cumulative cash flow from oil and gas sales is positive, taking into consideration the beginning cost pool, and all revenues and costs subsequent to January&#160;1, 2020.&#160;&#160;The maximum tax burden is equal to 25% of the cumulative cash flow and may be reduced or eliminated depending on the ratio of revenues to costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2015 Financial and Operational Outlook</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Each of the above factors has an impact on our financial condition and on our operations, either directly or indirectly.&#160;&#160;In response, we have taken the following steps in order to preserve capital, continue operations, and when possible, increase the amount of capital available to us:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Exploration and Production Segment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Gas Revenues</font>.&#160;&#160;Revenues from gas sales were $30.8 million during 2014, compared to $29.5 million and $30.3 million in 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;Our 2014 gas revenues increased $1.3 million from 2013 levels by approximately $0.8 million due to higher gas prices, coupled with approximately $0.5 million related to higher annual production.&#160;&#160;Our 2013 gas revenues decreased by $0.8 million from 2012 levels by approximately $1.7 million due to lower production, which was partially offset by $0.9 million in higher revenues due to higher gas prices.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Company-wide net gas production increased from a daily rate in 2013 of approximately 11.4 MMcfd to a rate of approximately 11.6 MMcfd in 2014, an increase of 2%.&#160;&#160;In mid-February 2015, gas was flowing in Poland at an average rate of 12.0 MMcfd, net to our interest.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Gas prices were 2.3% higher in 2014 than in 2013.&#160;&#160;The Polish low-methane tariff, which serves as the reference price for our gas sales agreements, was 3.0% higher during the full year of 2014 compared to 2013, due to an increase in the tariff that was effective January 1, 2014.&#160;&#160;Gas production at our Roszkow well, where we receive 95% of the low-methane tariff, declined from 38% of our total production in 2013 to 27% of our total production in 2014, which caused our average price per thousand cubic feet to decrease.&#160;&#160;Gas from our other producing Fences area wells is sold at a minimum of 86% of the tariff.&#160;&#160;The effect of exchange-rate changes between the U.S. dollar and Polish zloty on gas prices was minimal during 2014.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Gas production at our Kromolice-1, Sroda-4, and Kromolice-2, or KSK, wells averaged 9.7 MMcfd during 2014, compared to 11.1 MMcfd during 2013.&#160;&#160;At year-end, the wells were producing at a combined rate of 10.1 MMcfd.&#160;&#160;Gas at KSK is being sold to PGNiG at a contracted rate equal to 86% of the published low-methane tariff.&#160;&#160;We have a 49% interest in the KSK wells.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Gas production at our Roszkow well averaged 6.4 MMcfd during 2014, compared to 8.9 MMcfd during 2013.&#160;&#160;At year-end, the well was producing approximately 5.3 MMcfd.&#160;&#160;We plan to install compression equipment at the well during the second half of 2015 to maintain production levels at 5.8 MMcfd.&#160;&#160;Gas at Roszkow is being sold to PGNiG at a contracted rate equal to 95% of the published low-methane tariff.&#160;&#160;We have a 49% interest in the Roszkow well.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Gas production at our Zaniemysl well averaged approximately 2.0 MMcfd through the first six months of 2013, at which point it was terminated due to an influx of water.&#160;&#160;Sidetrack operations in early 2015, conducted to access additional gas accumulations that appeared to be present higher in the structure, were unsuccessful.&#160;&#160;Gas at Zaniemysl is sold to PGNiG at a contracted rate equal to 70% of the published low-methane tariff.&#160;&#160;We have a 24.5% interest in the Zaniemysl well.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Gas production at our Winna Gora well averaged 2.3 MMcfd during 2014, compared to 2.0 MMcfd during 2013.&#160;&#160;At year-end, the well was producing approximately 2.1 MMcfd.&#160;&#160;Gas at Winna Gora is being sold to PGNiG at a contracted rate equal to 86% of the published low-methane tariff.&#160;&#160;We have a 49% interest in the Winna Gora well.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Gas production began at our Lisewo-1 well in December of 2013 and at Lisewo-2 in September of 2014.&#160;&#160;At year-end, the Lisewo-1 well was producing at a rate of approximately 4.3 MMcfd, and the Lisewo-2 well was shut-in pending a workover.&#160;&#160;Following a successful workover in early 2015, the Lisewo wells were producing at a combined rate of 7.0 MMcfd. Gas at Lisewo is being sold to PGNiG at a contracted rate equal to 86% of the published low-methane tariff.&#160;&#160;We have a 49% interest in the Lisewo wells.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Oil Revenues</font>.&#160;&#160;Oil revenues were $3.5 million, $3.9 million, and $4.1 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;Lower production and oil prices in 2014 compared to 2013 caused the decrease in revenues.&#160;&#160;Higher average oil prices in 2013 compared to 2012 were offset by lower production to cause the decrease in revenues.&#160;&#160;Our average oil price during 2014 was $74.24 per barrel, a 7% decrease compared to $79.48 per barrel received during 2013.&#160;&#160;Production from our U.S. properties declined by 4% due to normal production declines.&#160;&#160;The current oil price environment will make most of our U.S. production uneconomic.&#160;&#160;However, due to high field-level pressures, it is problematic for us to shut-in more than a few wells at a time.&#160;&#160;As a consequence, we will likely see negative cash flows from our oil production until the oil price we receive returns to approximately $50 per barrel.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>U.S. oil revenues in 2014 decreased from 2013 levels by approximately $0.2 million due to lower oil prices, combined with approximately $0.2 million related to production declines.&#160;&#160;U.S. oil revenues in 2013 increased from 2012 levels by approximately $0.1 million due to higher oil prices, offset by approximately $0.3 million related to production declines.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Geological and geophysical costs, or G&amp;G costs, were $10.8 million, $14.1 million, and $11.1 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;During all three years, most of our G&amp;G costs were spent on acquiring, processing, and interpreting new 3-D and 2-D seismic data in the Fences, Edge, and other concession areas in Poland.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Exploratory dry-hole costs were $10.4 million, $6.7 million, and $12.7 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;Our 2014 dry-hole cost were associated with our Polish Baraniec-1 and Angowice-2 wells, along with some costs associated with an unsuccessful recompletion at our Szymanowice well that was drilled in 2013.&#160;&#160;Our 2013 dry-hole costs were associated with our Mieczewo-1K and Plawce-2 wells in Poland.&#160;&#160;Our 2012 dry-hole costs were associated primarily with our Kutno-2 well in Poland.&#160;&#160;The Kutno-2 well, which was the deepest well ever drilled in Poland, was found to be noncommercial during the third quarter of 2012.&#160;&#160;Total costs to us were approximately $12.2 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Impairment Costs</font>.&#160;&#160;Impairments of oil and gas properties were $23.3 million, $6.1 million, and $2.6 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;During 2014, as part of narrowing our operational focus in Poland moving forward, we dropped our concession blocks 246 and 287 and impaired the approximately $0.3 million concession costs associated with those blocks.&#160;&#160;In addition, we impaired approximately $9.2 million of costs associated with the Frankowo and Gorka Duchowna wells, located in Block 246.&#160;&#160;We also sold our interest in the Grabowka wells, located in Block 287, with costs totaling approximately $0.1 million.&#160;&#160;Finally, in Poland, we impaired prior-year costs at our Szymanowice and Komorze wells of $3.7 million and $7.1 million, respectively, as those wells were determined to be uneconomic during the year.&#160;&#160;In the United States, we reviewed our year-end oil reserves on a fair value basis, considering that current oil prices are much lower than the average prices used in our reserve report, which were determined using SEC pricing guidelines.&#160;&#160;Based on current and forecast oil prices, most of our oil reserves are uneconomic.&#160;&#160;The result of this review caused us to impair approximately $2.9 million of capital costs associated with our Montana producing properties.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>During 2013, we impaired approximately $4.5 million of prior-year costs associated with our Plawce-2 well following its unsuccessful fracture stimulation, along with approximately $0.2 million of prior-year costs associated with our Mieczewo-1K well.&#160;&#160;In addition, our Zaniemysl-3 well ceased production during 2013, causing us to charge its remaining net book value of $0.4 million to impairment expense.&#160;&#160;Finally, we recorded an impairment charge of $1.0 million related to concession costs in our Northwest and Warsaw South project areas, where we have dropped acreage that we believe is less prospective for oil and gas accumulations than retained areas.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>During 2012, we impaired $0.8 million in costs of certain concessions in Poland that we determined were not prospective.&#160;&#160;Also during 2012, we impaired all capitalized costs associated with our Alberta Bakken project in Montana, which included $1.4 million in drilling costs incurred during 2011 and $0.4 million in leasehold costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">DD&amp;A Expense&#8212;Producing Operations</font>.&#160;&#160;DD&amp;A expense for producing properties was $4.5 million, $3.6 million, and $3.1 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;The increase from 2013 to 2014 is a combination of higher DD&amp;A expenses due to increased production at our Lisewo wells, along with higher DD&amp;A expenses resulting from negative revisions in proved reserves at our Lisewo, Komorze, and Roszkow wells.&#160;&#160;The 16% increase from 2012 to 2013 is due primarily to new production from our Winna Gora and Lisewo-1 wells.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Future DD&amp;A costs are expected to generally, but not completely, follow future production trends.&#160;&#160;However, future DD&amp;A rates can be very different depending upon future capitalized costs and changes in reserve volumes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accretion Expense</font>.&#160;&#160;Accretion expense was $96,000, $90,000, and $63,000 for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;Accretion expense is related entirely to our asset retirement obligation associated with expected future plugging and abandonment costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Oilfield Services Revenues</font>.&#160;&#160;Oilfield services revenues were $3.8 million, $1.2 million, and $2.1 million for the years ended December 31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;We drilled 12 wells for third parties during 2014, along with additional well service work.&#160;&#160;We drilled three wells for third parties during 2013, along with additional well service work.&#160;&#160;During 2012, we drilled five wells for third parties, including one drilled for our Alberta Bakken joint venture, along with additional well service work.&#160;&#160;Oilfield services revenues will continue to fluctuate from period to period based on market demand, weather, the number of wells drilled, downtime for equipment repairs, the degree of emphasis on using our oilfield services equipment on our own properties, and other factors.&#160;&#160;We cannot accurately predict future oilfield services revenues.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Oilfield Services Costs.&#160;&#160;</font>Oilfield services costs were $2.5 million, $1.2 million, and $1.6 million for the years ended December 31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively, or 66%, 97%, and 76% of oilfield-servicing revenues, respectively.&#160;&#160;The changes in services costs from year to year were primarily due to the nature of our drilling activity discussed above, along with higher equipment repair costs in 2013.&#160;&#160;In general, oilfield-servicing costs are closely associated with oilfield services revenues.&#160;&#160;As such, oilfield services costs will continue to fluctuate period to period based on the number of wells drilled, revenues generated, weather, downtime for equipment repairs, the degree of emphasis on using our oilfield services equipment on our own properties, and other factors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">DD&amp;A Expense &#8211; Oilfield Services.&#160;&#160;</font>DD&amp;A expense for oilfield services was $1.0 million, $1.0 million, and $1.1 million for the years ended December 31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;We spent $0.8 million, $1.1 million, and $0.7 million on upgrading our oilfield-servicing equipment during 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">G&amp;A Costs&#8212;Corporate.&#160;&#160;</font>G&amp;A costs were $8.5 million, $8.8 million, and $8.4 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;The decrease in 2014 is primarily due to lower compensation costs.&#160;&#160;During 2013, compensation costs included the payment of a company-wide incentive award of approximately $500,000 related to 2008, which had been deferred until we met certain performance benchmarks, which were met in 2013.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Interest and Other (Income) Expense&#8212;Corporate</font>.&#160;&#160;Interest and other (income) expense was $2.7 million, $3.2 million, and $2.1 million for the years ended December 31, 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;During 2014, we incurred $2.8 million in interest expense, which included $0.5 million of amortization of loan fees and $0.4 million in unused commitment fees.&#160;&#160;Interest and other income expense was $0.1 million during 2014.&#160;&#160;During 2013, we recorded $1.2 million of amortization of loan fees, including $0.7 million related to our prior credit facility that was charged to interest expense by virtue of our refinance that year and $0.3 million in unused commitment fees.&#160;&#160;Interest and other income was $0.1 million during 2013.&#160;&#160;During 2012, we incurred $2.5 million in interest expense, which included $0.5 million of amortization of loan fees and $0.5 million in unused commitment fees.&#160;&#160;Interest and other income expense was $0.4 million during 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Extensions, Discoveries, and Other Additions</font>.&#160;&#160;All of the 2014 additions to proved reserves that resulted from the discovery of new fields are associated with our Karmin-1, Tuchola-3K, and Tuchola-4K wells in Poland.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Revisions</font>.&#160;&#160;Revisions represent changes in previous reserve estimates, either positive revisions upward or negative revisions downward, resulting from new information normally obtained from development drilling and production history or resulting from a change in economic factors, such as commodity prices, operating costs, or development costs.&#160;&#160;During 2014, excluding the volume reduction due to annual production, we recorded downward revisions at several of our producing wells in Poland.&#160;&#160;Significant downward revisions were recorded at our Szymanowice well, which we plugged in early 2014 following an unsuccessful sidetrack operation, and at our Komorze and Lisewo wells, whose downhole pressure dropped unexpectedly apparently due to compartmentalization issues.&#160;&#160;We also disposed of our Grabowka wells due to the large amount of time required to manage the wells compared to their marginal economics.&#160;&#160;These were partially offset by upward reserve revisions at our Roszkow and Kromolice South wells, where new pressure data indicates that the initial gas-in-place for these wells may be more than estimated at year-end 2013.&#160;&#160;We also recorded negative revisions of approximately 57,000 barrels of oil in the United States, primarily due to the reduction of economic barrels caused by lower oil prices and higher operating costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2012, excluding the volume reduction due to annual production, we recorded downward revisions at our Zaniemysl-3 and KSK wells due to, respectively, water influx and lower than expected wellhead pressures obtained during the fourth quarter of the year.&#160;&#160;These were partially offset by upward reserve revisions at our Roszkow, Lisewo-1, and Winna Gora wells, where new pressure data indicates that the initial gas-in-place for these wells may be more than estimated at year-end 2011.&#160;&#160;We also recorded upward revisions of approximately 9,000 barrels of oil in the United States, primarily due to lower operating costs resulting in more economically recoverable barrels.&#160;&#160;(See Items 1 and 2, Business and Properties).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Production</font>.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Gas Revenues&#8221; and &#8220;Oil Revenues&#8221; above.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2015 Operational Trends</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We currently expect that our 2015 production volume will rise slightly from our 2014 production rates with a full year of production at our Lisewo-2 well, which we believe will be greater than the natural declines in production from our currently producing wells.&#160;&#160;The amount of revenue from this increased production will depend on applicable gas sales prices and prevailing currency exchange rates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Future oil revenues from our domestic production will depend on the impact of prices we receive as we continue to experience normal production declines.&#160;&#160;We cannot accurately predict future oilfield services revenues and related costs, which will continue to fluctuate based on market demand, weather, the number of wells drilled, downtime for equipment repairs, the nature and extent of any equipment upgrading, the degree of emphasis on using our oilfield services equipment on our own properties, and other factors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Costs that vary in conjunction with production, such as lease operating expenses and DD&amp;A costs, will trend up or down with production increases or decreases.&#160;&#160;Our 2015 plans for capital expenditures are detailed in the following section, &#8220;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#8211;Our Capital Resources and Future Expenditures.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our U.S. dollar-denominated financial results will continue to be impacted by exchange-rate fluctuations, which cannot be predicted.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>For much of our history, we have financed our operations principally through the sale of equity securities, bank borrowings, and agreements with industry participants that funded our share of costs in certain exploratory activities in return for an interest in our properties.&#160;&#160;However, as our oil and gas production has increased in Poland in the last several years, our internally generated cash flow has become a significant source of operations financing.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2014 Liquidity and Capital</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Working Capital (current assets less current liabilities).</font>&#160;&#160;Our working capital was $17.1 million as of December 31, 2014, an increase of $5.8 million from December 31, 2013.&#160;&#160;The primary cause of the increase is the proceeds from our preferred stock offering.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>During 2014, we closed an underwritten public offering of 800,000 shares of our 9.25% Series B Cumulative Convertible Preferred Stock (the &#8220;Series B Preferred Stock&#8221;) at a public offering price of $25.00 per share.&#160;&#160;The aggregate gross proceeds from the offering were $20 million, with net proceeds, after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses, of approximately $18.4 million.&#160;&#160;Cumulative dividends of 9.25%, or $1.9 million per year, are payable out of funds legally available therefor.&#160;&#160;We are using the proceeds for exploration efforts in our Edge concession in Poland and for general corporate purposes, including declaring and paying dividends on our Series B Preferred Stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Operating Activities</font>.&#160;&#160;Net cash provided by operations during 2014 and 2013 was $2.1 million and $2.3 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Net cash used in operations during 2012 was $1.2 million.&#160;&#160;Cash flow from operating activities in both years benefited from positive change in working capital items.&#160;&#160;A $7.2 million increase in exploration costs offset higher revenues in 2012, leading to a decline in cash provided from operating activities in 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Investing Activities</font>.&#160;&#160;We used net cash in investing activities of $24.8 million, $27.9 million, and $16.3 million in 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;In 2014, we spent $16.6 million for oil and gas property additions, $16.0 million of which were related to our Polish drilling activities, with the remainder being spent on our domestic properties.&#160;&#160;Following the issuance of the Series B Preferred Stock, we purchased $7.4 million of marketable securities.&#160;&#160;We spent $0.9 million adding to our oilfield services equipment.&#160;&#160;In 2013, we spent $26.8 million for oil and gas property additions, $26.0 million of which were related to our Polish drilling activities, with the remainder being spent on our domestic properties.&#160;&#160;We also spent $1.1 million adding to our oilfield services equipment.&#160;&#160;In 2012, we spent $15.8 million for oil and gas property additions, all of which were related to our Polish drilling activities.&#160;&#160;We also spent $0.7 million adding to our oilfield services and office equipment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Financing Activities</font>.&#160;&#160;Our cash flow from financing activities was $23.6 million, $3.0 million, and $0 during 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.&#160;&#160;During 2014, as described above, we sold 800,000 shares of Series B Preferred Stock during 2014.&#160;&#160;After associated offering costs, the net proceeds from the offering were approximately $18.4 million, from which we paid preferred dividends of $0.4 million.&#160;&#160;We also sold 163,639 shares of common stock under our at-the-market agreement in connection with our existing shelf registration.&#160;&#160;Net proceeds from the stock sale were approximately $0.6 million after deducting associated costs.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>During 2013, we borrowed $43.0 million under our new credit facility, using $40 million to repay our 2010 credit facility and $2.0 million in fees associated with the new credit facility.&#160;&#160;There were no financing transactions during 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our Capital Resources and Future Expenditures</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our anticipated sources of liquidity and capital for 2015 include our working capital of $17.1 million at year-end 2014, credit that may be available under our Senior Secured Credit Facility, and cash available from our operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In July 2013, we finalized our Senior Secured Credit Facility with BNP Paribas (Suisse) SA and ING Bank N.V.&#160;&#160;The initial commitment of the facility amounts to $65 million.&#160;&#160;We can seek to increase the commitment up to $100 million under certain conditions via an embedded accordion mechanism.&#160;&#160;The credit facility calls for a periodic interest rate of LIBOR, plus an interest margin of 3.75% for the first three years of the facility and 4.00% for the final two years.&#160;&#160;The facility has a term of five years, with scheduled semiannual borrowing base reductions of $13 million beginning on June 30, 2016.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>As of December 31, 2014, we had $50 million outstanding under the facility and $5 million of available credit.&#160;&#160;We are discussing with our lenders an amendment and restatement of our existing facility, which would likely increase our borrowing base beyond the $55 million current level, which was set at our most recent redetermination.&#160;&#160;However, should these discussions not result in an increased borrowing base or revisions to the amortization language of the existing credit agreement, then we would likely have to begin amortization of our loan in 2015, which would be sooner than the scheduled commitment reductions outlined in our Senior Secured Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;This amortization would substantially impair the amount of capital we would have available for additional capital expenditures.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We have a history of operating losses, and we may continue to incur operating losses in future periods, as we continue to fund substantial exploration and development in Poland.&#160;&#160;From our inception in January 1989 through December 31, 2014, we have incurred cumulative net losses of approximately $258 million.&#160;&#160;Despite our production and revenues, our exploration and production activities may continue to result in net losses in future years, depending on the success of our drilling activities in Poland and the United States and whether we generate sufficient revenues to cover related operating expenses.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We may also seek to obtain additional funds for future capital investments from the sale of partial property interests or arrangements such as those negotiated in prior years for our Kutno and Warsaw South project areas in which industry participants are bearing the initial exploration costs to earn an interest in the project or other arrangements, all of which may dilute the interests of our existing stockholders or our interest in the specific project financed.&#160;&#160;Currently we are exploring such a farmout arrangement as a possible source of external capital for Tuchola production and related facilities and further exploration.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We will allocate our existing capital, as well as funds we may obtain in the future, among our various projects at our discretion.&#160;&#160;We may change the allocation of capital among the categories of anticipated expenditures depending upon future events.&#160;&#160;For example, we may change the allocation of our expenditures based on the actual results and costs of future exploration, appraisal, development, production, property acquisition, and other activities.&#160;&#160;In addition, we may have to change our anticipated expenditures if costs of placing any particular discovery into production are higher, if the field is smaller, or if the commencement of production takes longer than expected.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>During the ordinary course of business in Poland, we enter into agreements for the drilling of wells, the construction of production facilities, and for seismic projects.&#160;&#160;These are typically short-term agreements and are completed in less than one year.&#160;&#160;We are subject to certain work commitments respecting our 100%-owned exploration concessions that must be satisfied in order to maintain our interest in those concessions.&#160;&#160;These work commitments are optional on our part; however, they must be satisfied in order to maintain our interest in those concessions.&#160;&#160;We can request changes to usufruct and concession agreements that either modify the obligations to reduce our commitments or extend the terms of those agreements.&#160;&#160;In addition, we routinely relinquish acreage that we believe has lower potential rather than continue to be subject to the related work commitment.&#160;&#160;Our exploration budget and related activities are focused on exploration and long-term exploitation of our most promising exploration opportunities and are not specifically or primarily focused on meeting these work commitments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our oil and gas drilling and production operations are subject to hazards incidental to the industry that can cause severe damage to and destruction of property and equipment, pollution or environmental damage, suspension of operations, personal injury, and loss of life.&#160;&#160;To lessen the effects of these hazards, we maintain insurance of various types to cover our U.S. and Poland operations and also rely on the insurance or financial capabilities of our exploration partners in Poland.&#160;&#160;These measures do not cover risks related to violations of environmental laws or all other risks involved in oil and gas exploration, drilling, and production.&#160;&#160;We would be adversely affected by a significant event that is not fully covered by insurance or by our inability to maintain adequate insurance in the future at rates we consider reasonable.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Asset Retirement Obligation</font>.&#160;&#160;We have liabilities of $2.0 million related to asset retirement obligations on our Consolidated Balance Sheet at December&#160;31, 2014, excluded from the table above.&#160;&#160;Due to the nature of these obligations, we cannot determine precisely when the payments will be made to settle these obligations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">New Accounting Pronouncements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>On May 28, 2014, the Financial Accounting Standards Board issued ASU No. 2014-09, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</font>, which requires an entity to recognize the amount of revenue to which it expects to be entitled for the transfer of promised goods or services to customers.&#160;&#160;ASU 2014-09 will replace most existing revenue recognition guidance in U.S. generally accepted accounting principles when it becomes effective on January&#160;1, 2017.&#160;&#160;Early application is not permitted.&#160;&#160;The standard permits the use of either the retrospective or cumulative effect transition method.&#160;&#160;We are evaluating the effect that ASU 2014-09 will have on our consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.&#160;&#160;We have not yet selected a transition method or determined the effect of the standard on our ongoing financial reporting.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We have reviewed all other recently issued, but not yet adopted, accounting standards in order to determine their effects, if any, on our consolidated results of operations, financial position, and cash flows.&#160;&#160;Based on that review, we believe that none of these pronouncements will have a significant effect on current or future earnings or operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Critical Accounting Policies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Oil and Gas Activities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We follow the successful efforts method of accounting for our oil and gas properties.&#160;&#160;Under this method of accounting, all property acquisition costs and costs of exploratory and development wells are capitalized when incurred, pending determination of whether the well has found proved reserves.&#160;&#160;If an exploratory well has not found proved reserves, these costs plus the costs of drilling the well are expensed.&#160;&#160;The costs of development wells are capitalized, whether productive or nonproductive.&#160;&#160;Geological and geophysical costs on exploratory prospects and the costs of carrying and retaining unproved properties are expensed as incurred.&#160;&#160;An impairment allowance is provided to the extent that net capitalized costs of unproved properties, on a property-by-property basis, are not considered to be realizable.&#160;&#160;An impairment loss is recorded if the net capitalized costs of proved oil and gas properties exceed the aggregate undiscounted future net cash flows determined on a property-by-property basis.&#160;&#160;The impairment loss recognized equals the excess of net capitalized costs over the related fair value, determined on a property-by-property basis.&#160;&#160;Gains and losses are recognized on sales of entire interests in proved and unproved properties.&#160;&#160;Sales of partial interests are generally treated as a recovery of costs, and any resulting gain or loss is recorded as other income.&#160;&#160;Revenues associated with oil and gas sales are recorded when title passes, which is upon delivery to the pipeline or purchaser, and are net of royalties.&#160;&#160;Oilfield service revenues are recognized when the related service is performed.&#160;&#160;As a result of the foregoing, our results of operations for any particular period may not be indicative of the results that could be expected over longer periods.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Oil and Gas Reserves</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>All of the reserve data in this Form&#160;10-K are estimates.&#160;&#160;Estimates of our crude oil and natural gas reserves are prepared by our engineers in accordance with guidelines established by the Securities and Exchange Commission.&#160;&#160;Reservoir engineering is a subjective process of estimating underground accumulations of crude oil and natural gas.&#160;&#160;There are numerous uncertainties inherent in estimating quantities of proved crude oil and natural gas reserves.&#160;&#160;Uncertainties include the projection of future production rates and the expected timing of development expenditures.&#160;&#160;The accuracy of any reserve estimate is a function of the quality of available data and of engineering and geological interpretation and judgment.&#160;&#160;As a result, reserve estimates may be different from the quantities of crude oil and natural gas that are ultimately recovered.&#160;&#160;In addition, economic producibility of reserves is dependent on the oil and gas prices used in the reserve estimate.&#160;&#160;We based our December 31, 2014, reserve estimates on a 12-month average commodity price, unless contractual arrangements designated the price to be used, in accordance with Securities and Exchange Commission rules.&#160;&#160;However, oil and gas prices are volatile and, as a result, our reserve estimates will change in the future.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Estimates of proved crude oil and natural gas reserves significantly affect our DD&amp;A expense.&#160;&#160;For example, if estimates of proved reserves decline, the DD&amp;A rate will increase, resulting in a decrease in net income.&#160;&#160;A decline in estimates of proved reserves could also cause us to perform an impairment analysis to determine if the carrying amount of crude oil and natural gas properties exceeds fair value and could result in an impairment charge, which would reduce earnings.&#160;&#160;See Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&#8211;Supplemental Information.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stock-based Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Stock-based compensation cost is measured at the grant date, based on the estimated fair value of the award, and is recognized as expense over the employee&#8217;s requisite service period.</font></div>

<td valign="top" width="80%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ITEM 7A. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE</font></div>
</td>
</tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="80%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</font></div>
</td>
</tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="80%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Price Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Substantially all of our gas in Poland is sold to PGNiG or its affiliates under contracts that extend for the life of each field.&#160;&#160;Prices are determined contractually and, in the case of our producing wells in Poland, are tied to published tariffs.&#160;&#160;The tariffs are set from time to time by the public utility regulator in Poland.&#160;&#160;Although we are not directly subject to such tariffs, we have agreed to link our price to these tariffs in our contracts with PGNiG.&#160;&#160;We expect that the prices we receive in the short term for gas we produce will be lower than would be the case in an unregulated setting and may be lower than prevailing Western European prices.&#160;&#160;We believe it is more likely than not that, over time, the end user gas price in Poland will converge with the average price in Europe.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Realized pricing for our oil production in the United States is primarily driven by the prevailing worldwide price of oil, subject to gravity and other adjustments for the actual oil sold.&#160;&#160;Historically, oil prices have been volatile and unpredictable.&#160;&#160;Price volatility relating to our oil production is expected to continue in the foreseeable future.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We currently do not engage in any hedging activities to protect ourselves against market risks associated with oil and gas price fluctuations, although we may elect to do so in the future.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Foreign Currency Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We enter into various agreements in Poland denominated in the Polish zloty.&#160;&#160;The exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and the Polish zloty is subject to fluctuations that are beyond our control.&#160;&#160;During 2014, the zloty fluctuated between a low of 3.00 zlotys per dollar to a high of 3.55 zlotys per dollar, a fluctuation of 18%.&#160;&#160;Variations in exchange rates affect the dollar-denominated amount of revenue we receive in zlotys.&#160;&#160;As the dollar strengthens relative to the zloty, our dollar-denominated revenue received in zlotys declines; on the other hand, when the dollar weakens relative to the zloty, our dollar-denominated revenue received in zlotys increases.&#160;&#160;Conversely, a weak dollar leads to lower dollar-denominated drilling, capital, and exploration costs, while a strong dollar has the opposite effect for the cost structure of our Polish operations.&#160;&#160;Should exchange rates in effect during early 2015 continue throughout the year, we expect the exchange rates to have a negative impact on our dollar-denominated revenues compared to 2014.&#160;&#160;We are also generating revenues in Poland in zlotys, and we keep those zlotys in Poland and use them to pay zloty-based invoices.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Subsequent to year-end 2014, we entered into two separate dollar/zloty hedge agreements.&#160;&#160;The agreements are in the form of a costless collar, with floors of approximately 3.57 PLN/USD and ceilings of approximately 3.85 PLN/USD.&#160;&#160;One of the agreements, in the amount of $6.0 million, terminates on June 26, 2015, and the other, in the amount of $6.5 million, terminates on December 29, 2015.&#160;&#160;If on the settlement date of the agreements, the exchange rate is more than 3.85 PLN, the hedge will be terminated in our favor.&#160;&#160;If, on the other hand, the exchange rate is less than 3.57 PLN, we will be required to settle the difference.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We maintain disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports that we file or submit to the Securities and Exchange Commission under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, is recorded, processed, summarized, and reported within the periods specified by the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms, and that information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our principal executive and principal financial officers (whom we refer to in this periodic report as our Certifying Officers), as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.&#160;&#160;Our management evaluated, with the participation of our Certifying Officers, the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures as of December&#160;31, 2014, pursuant to Rule&#160;13a-15(b) under the Securities Exchange Act.&#160;&#160;Based upon that evaluation, our Certifying Officers concluded that, as of December&#160;31, 2014, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting that occurred during our most recently completed fiscal quarter that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Management of FX Energy, Inc., together with its consolidated subsidiaries (the Company), is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting.&#160;&#160;Our internal control over financial reporting is a process designed by our principal executive and principal financial officers to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of our financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>As of the end of our 2014 fiscal year, management conducted an assessment of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the framework established in the 2013 Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).&#160;&#160;Based on this assessment, management has determined that our internal control over financial reporting as of December&#160;31, 2014, was effective.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our internal control over financial reporting includes policies and procedures that: (1)&#160;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect transactions and dispositions of assets; (2)&#160;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and our directors; and (3)&#160;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of our assets that could have a material effect on our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Board of Directors and Shareholders</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FX Energy, Inc.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have audited the internal control over financial reporting of FX Energy, Inc. and subsidiaries (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) as of December 31, 2014, based on criteria established in the 2013 <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework</font> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management's Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.&#160;&#160;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&#160;&#160;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.&#160;&#160;Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&#160;&#160;We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&#160;&#160;A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&#160;&#160;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2014, based on criteria established in the 2013 <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework</font> issued by COSO.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated financial statements of the Company as of and for the year ended December 31, 2014, and our report dated March 16, 2015 expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements.</font></div>
